definition_zh: 直到；到……为止；直到……才；（否定句）直到……才
definition_en: up to the time when something happens or ends
core_image: 走廊尽头的灯一直亮着，亮到门开为止
scene: 母亲坐在客厅没关灯，说要等孩子进门她才去睡。 She waited in the hall until the last bus arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 until 是「直到……为止」（第 1 个义项：动作持续到某时）；句意为她在门厅一直等到末班车到达。走廊的灯亮到门开为止的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同义的较短形式，义为「直到」，口语中更常用
形近但不同源，义为「不合时宜的」（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

senses.title: Action that continues up to a point in time
senses.definition: used to say that an action goes on and stops at a certain time
senses.definitionCN: 表示动作持续进行，到某一时间停止
senses.example: The shop stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店开到九点。
senses.why: The word marks the end point of a stretch of time, and the thing before that point simply keeps going.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出一段时间的终点，在此之前的事情就一直在持续。

senses.title: Not before a certain time
senses.definition: used with a negative or in a question to mean not happening before a time
senses.definitionCN: 与否定或疑问连用，表示在某一时间之前没有发生
senses.example: He did not answer until the third knock.
senses.exampleCN: 直到敲第三下他才应门。
senses.why: If a line marks where something stops, then nothing has happened on the near side of it; this is the negative reading.
senses.whyCN: 既然一条线标出某事停止的地方，那么线这一侧就还什么都没发生，这正是否定用法。

senses.title: A limit set on a rule
senses.definition: used of rules and notices that last up to a stated point
senses.definitionCN: 用于规定或通告，表示有效到某一时点
senses.example: The office is closed until Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室关到星期一。
senses.why: A notice needs an end point, and the word supplies exactly the point where the rule stops.
senses.whyCN: 通告需要一个终点，这个词提供的正是规定停止的那一点。

senses.title: A change that finally comes
senses.definition: used when a state lasts and then finally gives way
senses.definitionCN: 表示某种状态一直持续，最后才改变
senses.example: The noise went on until someone complained.
senses.exampleCN: 吵闹一直继续，直到有人投诉才停。
senses.why: When a stretch is long, the moment it ends is also the moment something turns, so the word gathers a sense of turning.
senses.whyCN: 当这一段很长时，它结束的那一刻也正是事情转折的一刻，于是这个词带上了转折意味。

senses.title: Until then in narrative
senses.definition: used in stories for the time before an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 在叙述中指某事发生之前的那段时间
senses.example: Until that night, nobody in the village locked a door.
senses.exampleCN: 在那晚之前，村里没人锁门。
senses.why: In a story the same end point can be read backwards, naming all the time before the event arrives.
senses.whyCN: 在故事里，同一个终点也可以反着读，指事件到来之前的整段时间。

intro.en: An old compound preposition whose first part survives in our northern word for the same thing.
intro.cn: 一个古老的复合介词，其前一部分仍保存在同义的北方说法里。

items.en: The form und means up to, and the older Scandinavian words spread it into English.
items.cn: und 意为「直到」，更早的斯堪的纳维亚语形式把它带进英语。

items.en: Till was already used for up to a time, and it is not a shortened form of until.
items.cn: till 早已表示「直到」，它并不是 until 的缩写。

items.en: Untill appears as a reinforced till, with un- here meaning up to rather than not.
items.cn: untill 作为加强形式的 till 出现，此处 un- 意为「直到」，并非否定。

items.en: Until and till are used side by side, until being more formal in writing.
items.cn: until 与 till 并行使用，写作中 until 更正式。

items.en: Not until opens a clause and forces the main verb to come late, a favourite of formal prose.
items.cn: not until 引导从句并使主动词后置，是正式文章偏爱的结构。

note.en: The look-alike group collects time prepositions and similar spellings, while the near-meaning group compares end points.
note.cn: 形近组收集时间介词与相近拼写，近义组比较表示终点的时间词。

entries.definition: from a time in the past until now
entries.definitionCN: 自……以来

normalIntro.en: A short, very old time word whose shape looks like a negative but is not one.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短而古老的表示时间的词，它的样子像否定，其实不是。

normal.en: Until and till are equally old; neither is a clipping of the other.
normal.cn: until 与 till 一样古老，谁也不是谁截出来的。

normal.en: Not until with an inverted main clause is the formal pattern.
normal.cn: not until 加倒装主句是正式模式。

normal.en: From morning until night shows the stretch of time clearly.
normal.cn: from morning until night 清楚显示了时间的段距。

normal.en: Until further notice is the fixed phrase in notices.
normal.cn: until further notice 是通告里的固定说法。

normal.en: The un- here means up to, unlike un- in unhappy.
normal.cn: 此处的 un- 意为「直到」，不同于 unhappy 中的 un-。

abstract.en: Watch a hallway light burn until a door opens.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊的灯一直亮着，直到门打开。

abstract.en: Count three knocks before the chain is lifted.
abstract.cn: 数到第三下敲门声，链子才被摘下。

abstract.en: See a line drawn on a road, and a car stopping at it.
abstract.cn: 看路面上画着一条线，一辆车停在线上。

examples.en: We waited at the gate until the lights went out.
examples.cn: 我们在门口一直等到灯灭。

examples.en: She did not speak until the whole room was quiet.
examples.cn: 直到整个房间安静下来，她才开口。

examples.en: The road will stay closed until the bridge is repaired.
examples.cn: 这条路将封闭到桥梁修好为止。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺踢了」——等得实在不耐烦，俺踢了踢门框，一直踢到门开为止。

root: 中古英语 untill，由上古北欧语 und（直到）与 till（到……为止）结合而成；till 本身并非 until 的缩略，二者同义并行

sensesIntro.en: One function, marking the end of a stretch of time, yields the durative sense and the negative sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个功能「标出一段时间的终点」，生出持续义与否定义两路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright line drawn on a road.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上一条亮着的线。

branches.en: The duration branch: something goes on all the way there.
branches.cn: 持续分支：某事一路持续到那一点。

branches.en: The negative branch: nothing happens on the near side.
branches.cn: 否定分支：线这一侧什么都没发生。

branches.en: The notice branch: rules that last to a stated point.
branches.cn: 通告分支：规定有效到某个时点。

branches.en: The turning branch: a long state at last gives way.
branches.cn: 转折分支：长久的状态终于让位。

branches.en: The narrative branch: the stretch before an event.
branches.cn: 叙述分支：事件之前的那段时光。

intro.en: A small function word made of two old time markers fused together.
intro.cn: 一个由两个古老时间标记融合而成的小功能词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin adverb for up to this point is tenus, used with a genitive.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语中表示「到此为止」的副词是 tenus，与属格连用。

items.example: Until keeps the older sense of un as up to.
items.exampleCN: until 保留了 un 意为「直到」的古义。

items.example: Not until noon did it stop raining.
The office is closed until further notice.
items.exampleCN: 办公室关闭，直到另行通知。

items.example: Up until last week he was here.
items.exampleCN: 一直到上周他都在这里。

definition_zh: 覆盖；盖住；包括；掩护
definition_en: to put something over or on top; to include or deal with a range of things
core_image: 一块布或一个盖子压在上面的画面
scene: 要下雨了，妈妈快步走到阳台，把晾着的被子搬了进来。 Please cover the fish bowl before the cat arrives.
sceneCN: 这里 cover 是「盖住」（第 1 个义项：把东西放在上面遮住）；句意是猫来之前请把鱼缸盖上。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -age 构成，义为「覆盖范围；新闻报道量」
由 dis- 加 cover 构成，义为「发现」
由 re- 加 cover 构成，义为「恢复；找回」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「覆盖物」

senses.title: To put something over the top
senses.definition: to place something over or in front of another thing so it is hidden or protected
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在另一物的上面或前面，使其被遮住或受到保护
senses.example: Cover the leftovers before you put them in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 把剩菜盖好再放进冰箱。
senses.why: The core image is a lid or cloth pressed down over a thing, so any act of shielding from above is cover.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是盖子或布压在东西上方，所以一切自上而下的遮盖都可以叫 cover。

senses.title: To include a range of topics or areas
senses.definition: to deal with or contain many things within one range
senses.definitionCN: 在一个范围内处理或包含多种事物
senses.example: This chapter covers how plants make food.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章讲的是植物如何制造养分。
senses.why: A big cloth lies across the whole table; in the same way, one word or lesson may lie across many topics.
senses.whyCN: 一块大布铺满整张桌子；同样，一个词或一节课也能铺满许多话题。

senses.title: To protect or hide for someone
senses.definition: to protect a person or keep them from being seen or blamed
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人，或使其不被发现、不被责怪
senses.example: Our keeper moved quickly to cover the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员迅速移动去封堵球门。
senses.why: Sheltering under cover keeps a soldier safe, so helping someone by standing between them and danger is also covering.
senses.whyCN: 躲在掩体下能让士兵安全，所以站到别人与危险之间保护他们也是 covering。

senses.title: To report an event as a journalist
senses.definition: to follow and report news about an event
senses.definitionCN: 对某事件进行跟踪报道
senses.example: Two school reporters covered the sports meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两名校园记者报道了运动会。
senses.why: News spreads over the whole surface of an event like a sheet laid over it, so journalists cover events.
senses.whyCN: 新闻像铺在事件上的一层布覆盖全局，所以记者们「覆盖」事件。

intro.en: Cover traces back to Latin words about catching and covering over.
intro.cn: cover 可追溯到拉丁语中与「捕获、覆罩」相关的词。

items.en: The Latin co-operire meant to cover completely, with co- (together) plus operire (to cover).
items.cn: 拉丁语 co-operire 意为完全盖住，由 co-（一起）加 operire（覆盖）构成。

items.en: A related word capere, to seize, is thought by some scholars to be mixed in; the exact link is debated.
items.cn: 一些学者认为相关词 capere（抓住）也掺入其中；具体联系尚有争议。

items.en: Old French formed covrir, meaning to cover or protect.
items.cn: 古法语形成 covrir，意为覆盖、保护。

items.en: English borrowed coveren in the thirteenth century, meaning to cover over.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 coveren，意为盖上。

items.en: The noun cover for book covers and lids appeared later, and the verb spread to news and ranges.
items.cn: 名词 cover 指书皮和盖子出现较晚，动词义扩展到新闻和范围。

note.en: These words share the cover root or name things that hide or lie on top.
note.cn: 这些词与 cover 同根，或指遮盖、覆在上面的东西。

entries.definition: to wrap completely; also a paper holder
entries.definitionCN: 包裹；信封

normalIntro.en: The cover family and daily covers make the word stick.
normalIntro.cn: cover 词族和身边的「盖」让这个词扎根。

normal.en: co- + operire: cover fully, so cover means put over.
normal.cn: co- 加 operire：完全盖上，所以 cover 意为盖上。

normal.en: dis-cover: take the cover away, so discover means find.
normal.cn: dis-cover：把盖子拿走，所以 discover 意为发现。

normal.en: re-cover: cover again, so recover means get back.
normal.cn: re-cover：再盖回来，所以 recover 意为恢复、找回。

normal.en: Be covered with snow: the passive shows what lies on top.
normal.cn: be covered with snow：被动式说明上面盖着什么。

normal.en: The front cover of a notebook is the lid of the pages.
normal.cn: 笔记本的封面就是书页的盖子。

abstract.en: Watch a tablecloth slide across the table until no wood shows.
abstract.cn: 看桌布滑过桌面，直到一点木头都不露。

abstract.en: Snow falls all night; in the morning the field is one white cover.
abstract.cn: 雪下了一夜，清晨的田野变成一整块白色的盖子。

abstract.en: One quiz question may cover three chapters at once.
abstract.cn: 一道测验题可能同时覆盖三章内容。

examples.en: The ground was covered with yellow leaves after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，地面铺满了黄叶。

examples.en: Our report covers the school sports meeting.
examples.cn: 我们的报告报道了校运动会。

examples.en: Mom asked me to cover the pot so the soup stays warm.
examples.cn: 妈妈让我把锅盖上，让汤保持温热。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡我」——一张大卡「卡」住我，把我盖住了

root: 来自拉丁语 co-operire（完全覆盖，co-「一起」+ operire「盖上」），经古法语 covrir 进入英语；与 discover、recover 等构成「盖上—揭开—复原」的词族。

sensesIntro.en: From a lid over a pot, to topics under one range, to news over an event.
sensesIntro.cn: 从锅盖，到一个范围下的多个话题，再到铺满事件的新闻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lid pressed down over something
core.cn: 核心意象：一个盖子压在东西上面

branches.en: Cloths, lids and snow on top
branches.cn: 布、盖子和积雪覆在上面
一个范围容纳许多话题

branches.en: Standing between a friend and harm
Cover as shelter, not concealment only
branches.cn: cover 作为掩体，不只是藏匿

intro.en: Cover sits at the middle of a family of pre-verbed cousins.
intro.cn: cover 位于一组加前缀动词词族的中间。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root operire means to cover over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 operire 意为盖上、覆住。

definition_zh: 孙子；外孙
definition_en: the son of one's son or daughter
core_image: 隔一代的儿子：你孩子生的男孩，追着球跑出院门
scene: 球场边老人举着水壶等休息的哨声。 His grandson plays football every Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 grandson 是「孙子」（第 1 个义项：子女的儿子）；句意为他的孙子每周六都踢足球。

pos.zh: 名词：孙子；外孙（特指男性孙辈）

derivatives.zh: 对应的女性孙辈词
不分性别的上位词
复合词来源词，指儿子

senses.title: A son of your child
senses.definition: a boy child of your son or daughter
senses.definitionCN: 你儿子或你女儿所生的男孩
senses.example: Her grandson helped carry the heavy bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她的孙子帮忙提沉重的袋子。
senses.why: The core image is the second-generation son: grand plus son.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是隔一代的儿子：grand 加 son。

senses.title: A young male treated like family
senses.definition: a boy treated with grandfatherly affection though not a blood grandson
senses.definitionCN: 虽无血缘却受到长辈疼爱的男孩
senses.example: The old coach treats every player as a grandson.
senses.exampleCN: 老教练把每个队员都当孙儿看待。
senses.why: Affection again stretches the kinship word beyond blood.
senses.whyCN: 亲情再一次把称谓拉伸出血缘之外。

intro.en: Grandson is the shortest and oldest-shaped grand- compound.
intro.cn: grandson 是 grand- 复合词中最短、构型最老的一个。

items.en: Latin grandis meant large or grown.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为大、成年。

items.en: Old French grand entered English kinship words.
items.cn: 古法语 grand 进入英语亲属词。

items.en: Old English sunu meant son, a deep Germanic word.
items.cn: 古英语 sunu 指儿子，是极深的日耳曼词。

items.en: The compound grandson appears in Middle English family texts.
items.cn: 中古英语家庭文本中已见 grandson。

items.en: Grandson standardizes as the male grandchild word.
items.cn: 现代英语中 grandson 定型为男性孙辈词。

note.en: Grandson sits opposite granddaughter on the family tree.
note.cn: grandson 在家谱上与 granddaughter 相对而坐。

entries.definition: a sibling's son, one generation closer
entries.definitionCN: 侄子或外甥，血缘近一代

normalIntro.en: Five hooks for the boy on the family tree.
normalIntro.cn: 家族树上男孩的五条钩子。

normal.en: Grandson is grand + son, said in one breath.
normal.cn: grandson 是 grand 加 son，一口气读完。

normal.en: The eldest grandson carries the family banner.
normal.cn: 长孙举着家族的旗。

normal.en: Grandsons inherit their grandfather's watch.
normal.cn: 孙子们继承祖父的怀表。

normal.en: Son is hidden inside grandson.
normal.cn: son 就藏在 grandson 里。

normal.en: Grandson and granddaughter together make grandchildren.
normal.cn: grandson 加 granddaughter 合成 grandchildren。

abstract.en: A grandson is yesterday's watch on tomorrow's wrist.
abstract.cn: 孙儿是戴在明天手腕上的昨天怀表。

abstract.en: The football flies farther each year he grows.
abstract.cn: 他长大一岁，足球就飞得更远。

abstract.en: Two generations chase one ball across the yard.
abstract.cn: 两代人在院子里追同一颗球。

examples.en: My grandson is learning to swim this summer.
examples.cn: 我孙子今年夏天在学游泳。

examples.en: The grandfather walked his grandson to the bus stop.
examples.cn: 祖父送孙子去公交站。

examples.en: Both grandsons were named after their grandfathers.
examples.cn: 两个孙子都以祖父的名字命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歌兰森」——隔一代的男丁像森林里新长的树；grandson 就是家谱上新的一棵树

root: grand（拉丁 grandis「大」，表隔一代）+ son（古英语 sunu「儿子」，日耳曼词根）；复合称谓词。

sensesIntro.cn: 单一精确亲属义，外加一个亲情的延伸义。

definition_zh: 使厌烦；钻孔；令人厌烦的人；口径
definition_en: to make someone feel tired and uninterested, to make a hole, or the width of a gun barrel
core_image: 钻头一点点钻进木板，木屑顺着螺旋退出
scene: 木工把钻头对准木板，机器转动，一个圆孔慢慢钻了出来。 The drill bored a neat hole in the wood.

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to make someone feel tired and uninterested because something is dull
senses.definitionCN: 因为事情乏味而让人感到疲倦、提不起兴趣
senses.example: The long talk bored the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 那场冗长的讲话让全班都很厌烦。
senses.why: The dull sense grew in the eighteenth century from the idea of wearing a person down, like a drill wearing through wood.
senses.whyCN: 「乏味」这个义项在十八世纪出现，来自把人一点点磨下去的意思，像钻头磨穿木头。

senses.title: To make a hole
senses.definition: to make a round hole in something with a drill or similar tool
senses.definitionCN: 用钻具或类似工具在某物上打出圆孔
senses.example: They bored a hole in the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在墙上钻了一个孔。
senses.why: Old English borian meant to pierce, and making a hole is the oldest sense of this word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 borian 意为刺穿，打孔是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: A dull person
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes others feel tired and uninterested
senses.definitionCN: 让别人感到疲倦、提不起兴趣的人或事物
senses.example: He is a bore at every party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每个聚会上都是个乏味的人。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, so the person who bores others is simply called a bore.
senses.whyCN: 动词变成名词，于是让别人厌烦的人就直接被叫作 a bore。

senses.title: The width of a barrel
senses.definition: the inside width of a gun barrel or of a tube
senses.definitionCN: 枪管或管子的内部直径
senses.example: The gun has a narrow bore.
senses.exampleCN: 这把枪的口径很窄。
senses.why: The width of a barrel is the width of the hole bored through it, so bore also names that measure.
senses.whyCN: 枪管的宽度就是钻穿它的孔的宽度，所以 bore 也指这个尺寸。

intro.en: Bore began as a word for piercing a hole, and the sense of wearying someone came much later.
intro.cn: bore 最初指钻孔，而「使人厌烦」这个义项要晚得多才出现。

items.en: Old English borian meant to pierce or make a hole, and it is the oldest layer of the word.
items.cn: 古英语 borian 意为刺穿或打孔，这是这个词最古老的一层。

items.en: German bohren and Dutch boren are relatives, all meaning to drill or pierce.
items.cn: 德语 bohren 与荷兰语 boren 是同源词，都表示钻或刺穿。

items.en: In the eighteenth century bore gained the sense of wearying a person, probably from wearing someone down.
items.cn: 十八世纪 bore 有了「使人疲倦」的意思，可能来自把人一点点磨下去的说法。

items.en: The verb then produced the noun bore for a dull person or task.
items.cn: 动词随后产生名词 bore，指乏味的人或事。

items.en: Today bore covers drilling, digging tunnels, boring people and the width of a barrel.
items.cn: 今天 bore 覆盖钻孔、挖隧道、使人厌烦以及枪管口径。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape or sound; the near-meaning group collects words for drilling and dullness.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近的词；近义组收与钻孔、乏味有关的词。

entries.definition: Not covered by clothes or anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「赤裸的；空的」，拼写与 bore 相近。

entries.definition: Brought into life, used with be.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「出生的」，拼写与 bore 相近。

entries.definition: A tool for making holes, or to make a hole with it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「钻；钻孔」，对应 bore 的钻孔义。

entries.definition: A long passage dug under the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「隧道」，与 bore a tunnel 相关。
形容词，义为「乏味的；暗淡的」，对应 bore 的厌烦义。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English borian meant to pierce, and drilling a hole is the oldest sense.
normal.cn: 古英语 borian 意为刺穿，打孔是最古老的义项。

normal.en: German bohren and Dutch boren are relatives, all meaning to drill.
normal.cn: 德语 bohren 与荷兰语 boren 是同源词，都表示钻。

normal.en: The weary sense came in the eighteenth century, like wearing a person down.
normal.cn: 「使人厌烦」的义项在十八世纪出现，就像把人一点点磨下去。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with hole, tunnel, tears and gun.
normal.cn: 它常与 hole、tunnel、tears、gun 搭配。

normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-r-e，中间的 ore 读得像 more 里的 o。

abstract.en: See a drill turn into a board and leave a clean round hole: that is bore.
abstract.cn: 想象钻头钻进木板，留下一个整齐的圆孔：那就是 bore。

abstract.en: Feel the same long drill of a dull speech, and the word turns into weariness.
abstract.cn: 把同样的「长钻」换成一场冗长乏味的讲话，这个词就变成了厌倦。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the turning drill bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让转动的钻头把意思带回来。

examples.en: The long talk bored the whole class.
examples.cn: 那场冗长的讲话让全班都很厌烦。

examples.en: They bored a hole in the wall.
examples.cn: 他们在墙上钻了一个孔。

examples.cn: 他在每个聚会上都是个乏味的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波尔」——钻头一转就钻出个圆孔：钻孔

root: bore 有两个关系密切的意思来源。最古老的一层来自古英语 borian，意为刺穿、打孔，德语 bohren 与荷兰语 boren 是同源词；由钻穿的意思又引申出枪管「口径」。十八世纪这个词有了「使人疲倦」的意思，可能来自把人一点点磨下去的说法，随后产生名词 bore，指乏味的人或事。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bore rest on one picture: a drill turning into a hard surface, which can make a hole, a barrel width, or a wearisome experience.
sensesIntro.cn: bore 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：钻头钻进硬表面，它可以打出一个孔、量出一个口径，也可以变成一段把人磨得疲惫的经历。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drill turning into a board, with shavings curling out
core.cn: 核心意象：钻头钻进木板，木屑顺着螺旋退出

branches.en: THE WEARINESS: making a person tired is the youngest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 厌倦线：使人疲倦是这个词最年轻的义项。

branches.en: THE HOLE: piercing a surface is the oldest and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 孔洞线：刺穿表面是最古老、最身体化的义项。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a dull person takes the name of the feeling they cause.
branches.cn: 人物线：乏味的人得到了他们所造成的那种感觉的名字。

branches.en: THE WIDTH: the barrel measure is the width of the bored hole.
branches.cn: 口径线：枪管的尺寸就是被钻出的孔的宽度。

branches.en: THE DRILL: the tool links the act of piercing and the width it leaves.
branches.cn: 钻具线：钻具把「打孔」与「留下的孔径」连在一起。

intro.en: Bore is a base verb and noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: bore 是基础动词兼名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin terebrare and perforare are recorded verbs for boring through; they are parallels, not the source of bore.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terebrare 与 perforare 是有记录的「钻孔」动词，它们是平行词，不是 bore 的来源。

items.example: Borian is the recorded Old English source.
items.exampleCN: borian 是有记录的古英语来源。

items.example: It forms bore someone to tears.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 bore someone to tears。

items.example: It forms the bore of a gun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 the bore of a gun。

definition_zh: 意图；打算；目的
definition_en: a plan or aim in your mind before you act
core_image: 拉满却未放的弓：目标已定在弦上
scene: 少年攒了半年的零花钱，盯着橱窗里的望远镜。 She has every intention of finishing the course.
sceneCN: 这里 intention 是「打算」（第 1 个义项：心中的计划）；句意：她完全打算修完这门课。

collocations.phrase: the road to ruin is paved with good intentions

derivatives.zh: intention 的动词基，义为「打算；想要」
intend 加过去分词后缀，义为「预期的；想要的」
同源名词，义为「意图」（法律语境常用）

senses.title: A plan held in the mind
senses.definition: an aim or plan you hold before acting
senses.definitionCN: 行动之前心中所持的目标或计划
senses.example: Her intention was to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她的打算是出国留学。
senses.why: The bow is drawn but not released.
senses.whyCN: 弓已拉满，箭未离弦。

senses.title: A purpose behind an action
senses.definition: the purpose that an action serves
senses.definitionCN: 行为所服务的目的
senses.example: The remark carried no bad intention.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话并无恶意。
senses.why: The drawn bow explains the aimed arrow.
senses.whyCN: 拉满的弓解释了箭的去向。

senses.title: Good intentions gone wrong
senses.definition: kind plans that fail in practice
senses.definitionCN: 实践中落空的好心计划
senses.example: His good intentions paved a bumpy road.
senses.exampleCN: 他的好心铺了条颠簸路。
senses.why: The string snaps though the aim was kind.
senses.whyCN: 弦断了，尽管箭头原是善意的。

senses.title: Legal intent in writing
senses.definition: a declared aim, formal or legal use
senses.definitionCN: 正式或法律语境中的声明目标
senses.example: The letter states the buyer's intentions.
senses.exampleCN: 信中写明买方的意向。
senses.why: The bow is signed on paper.
senses.whyCN: 弓被签在了纸上。

intro.en: Intention comes from Latin intendere, to stretch toward, from in- (toward) and tendere (to stretch). An intention is a mind stretched toward a target.
intro.cn: intention 来自拉丁语 intendere「朝……张紧」，由 in-「朝向」+ tendere「拉伸」构成；intention 就是朝目标张紧的心。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch; it gave tendon, tense and tent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为拉伸；同根词有 tendon、tense、tent。

items.en: in- plus tendere formed intendere: to stretch toward a mark.
items.cn: in- 加 tendere 构成 intendere：朝目标张紧。

items.en: intentio meant the stretching, then the mental aim.
items.cn: intentio 先指拉伸，后指心中之志。

items.en: Old French entencion carried both attention and aim.
items.cn: 古法语 entencion 兼指专注与目标。

items.en: Middle English entencioun settled on the mental aim.
items.cn: 中古英语 entencioun 落定于心中目标。

items.en: Modern English kept the drawn-bow image in every sense.
items.cn: 现代英语在各义中保留了拉满之弓的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the stretch-root family. The meaning group compares words of plans.
note.cn: 形近组收录「拉伸」词根词族；词义组比较计划类词。

entries.definitionCN: 法律语境的意图孪生词。
朝某物张紧的注意力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the stretched-bow image, the tend root and the good-intentions proverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用张满之弓意象、tend 词根与好心谚语。

normal.en: in- plus tendere (stretch): mind pulled toward a target.
normal.cn: in- 加 tendere（拉伸）：心被拉向目标。

normal.en: tendon and tense share the stretching root.
normal.cn: tendon 与 tense 共享拉伸词根。

normal.en: with the intention of plus verb-ing.
normal.cn: with the intention of 后接动名词。

normal.en: good intentions can pave a bumpy road.
normal.cn: 好心也能铺出颠簸路。

normal.en: attention is the same bow aimed at a lesson.
normal.cn: attention 是瞄准课堂的同一张弓。

abstract.en: One image: a bow fully drawn, arrow not yet flown.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：弓已拉满，箭未离弦。

abstract.en: Every act is an arrow; intention is the drawn string.
abstract.cn: 行为是箭，intention 是那根拉紧的弦。

abstract.en: The target does not see the bow, only the arrow.
abstract.cn: 靶子看不见弓，只看见箭。

examples.en: He opened the shop with the intention of helping locals.
examples.cn: 他开店的本意是帮街坊。

examples.en: I have no intention of quitting.
examples.cn: 我无意放弃。

examples.en: Good intentions alone do not finish projects.
examples.cn: 光有善意完不成项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因ten申」：心中已有ten分打算，郑重申明， intention。

root: 拉丁语 in-「朝向」+ tendere「拉伸」→ intendere「朝目标张紧」→ intentio「心中之志」→ 古法语 entencion → 中古英语 entencioun → 现代英语 intention；同根词 tendon、tense、attention。

sensesIntro.en: Intention is the drawn bow: a plan held before action, the purpose behind the arrow, kind strings that snap, and a bow signed on paper.
sensesIntro.cn: intention 是拉满的弓：行动前的盘算、箭背后的目的、会断的善意之弦，以及签在纸上的弓。

core.en: A bow drawn toward a target before the arrow flies.

intro.en: Intention builds intend, intended and keeps intent in law.
intro.cn: intention 构成 intend、intended，法律语境保留 intent。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the stretching verb tendere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的拉伸动词 tendere。

definition_zh: 粗心的；漫不经心的；不在乎的
definition_en: not taking enough care, so that mistakes happen or feelings are hurt
core_image: 作业本上歪歪扭扭，橡皮屑和错字撒了一页
scene: 数学测验发下来，那道题只因粗心抄错一个数字就丢了分。 He lost two points in the maths test for one careless mistake.
sceneCN: 这里 careless 是「粗心的」（第 1 个义项：不留神而常出错）；句意为数学测验因粗心丢了两分。

pos.zh: 粗心的；漫不经心的；随便的

derivatives.zh: 由 careless 加 -ly 构成，义为「粗心地」
由 careless 加 -ness 构成，义为「粗心大意」

senses.title: Not paying enough attention
senses.definition: not taking enough care, so mistakes happen
senses.definitionCN: 不够留神，因而出错
senses.example: A careless mistake cost him the game.
senses.exampleCN: 一次疏忽让他输掉了比赛。
senses.why: The suffix -less takes the care away, leaving hands that forget to watch.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 把「心」拿走，只剩忘了看路的手。

senses.title: Not worrying or caring
senses.definition: showing no interest or concern
senses.definitionCN: 显得毫不在意
senses.example: He gave a careless shrug.
senses.exampleCN: 他满不在乎地耸耸肩。
senses.why: When care is absent, both mistakes and cold shoulders follow.
senses.whyCN: 「心」一缺席，错误与冷淡便接踵而来。

intro.en: Careless is care wearing the minus sign -less.
intro.cn: careless 就是 care 戴上了减号 -less。

items.en: Old English caru again means the heavy mind.
items.cn: 古英语 caru 又一次指沉重的心。

items.en: Middle English carlees meant free from anxiety, even a good thing then.
items.cn: 中古英语 carlees 本指无忧，甚至曾是褒义。

items.en: The suffix -less means without, from Old English leas.
items.cn: 后缀 -less 意为「无」，源自古英语 leas。

items.en: The sense slid from carefree to negligent.
items.cn: 词义从「无忧」滑向「疏忽」。

items.en: Today careless blames mistakes and cold manners alike.
items.cn: 今天 careless 既责疏忽，也责冷淡。

note.en: The first group collects family opposites and twins; the second collects negligence words.
note.cn: 第一组收同族反义词与形近词，第二组收疏忽类词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「小心的」，是反义词。
形容词，义为「不停的」，拼写与 careless 相近。
形容词，义为「坐立不安的」，同用 -less。

entries.definition: Failing to take proper care, formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「疏忽的」，正式用语。
形容词，义为「欠考虑的；不为他人着想」。
形容词，义为「鲁莽的」，程度更重。

normalIntro.en: Remember careless as care minus less.
normalIntro.cn: 把 careless 看成 care 减去 less。

normal.en: careless = care + less, care taken away.
normal.cn: careless 即「把小心拿走」。

normal.en: a careless mistake is easy to fix but hard to notice.
normal.cn: 粗心的错误好改却难察觉。

normal.en: carefully is the opposite adverb.
normal.cn: carefully 是它的反义副词。

normal.en: careless about clothes means untidy dressing.
normal.cn: careless about clothes 指穿得马虎。

normal.en: restless uses the same -less ending.
normal.cn: restless 用同样的 -less 后缀。

abstract.en: See a page of homework full of crossed-out numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一页作业划满了改错的数字。

abstract.en: Hear a door slam behind someone who did not look back.
abstract.cn: 听身后门砰地关上，那人头也不回。

abstract.en: Feel one step skipped on the stairs and the stumble after.
abstract.cn: 楼梯上跳了一级，随后一个踉跄。

examples.en: Careless driving causes many accidents.
examples.cn: 疏忽驾驶导致许多事故。

examples.en: His careless words hurt her feelings.
examples.cn: 他随口的话伤了她。

examples.en: The teacher circled every careless mistake.
examples.cn: 老师把每个粗心错误都圈了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凯尔利斯」——凯尔「累死」了，作业全是粗心错。

root: care（挂念）+ -less（无）→ careless；同族 careful、carelessness、carelessly；-less 族词 endless、useless、restless。

sensesIntro.en: Careless is the hole where care should be: mistakes first, indifference after.
sensesIntro.cn: careless 是「心」缺席留下的洞：先是错误，继而是冷淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that forgot to watch
core.cn: 核心意象：忘了看路的一双手

definition_zh: 等级；年级；成绩；评分；给……评级
definition_en: a level of quality, a school year, a mark for work, or to sort things by rank
core_image: 一级一级的台阶：按高低把东西排开
scene: 期末考试结束，老师在成绩单上写下每个学生的分数。 The teacher graded every essay before the holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 grade 是「评分；打分」（第 4 个义项：给作业评定等级）；句意为老师在假期前给每篇作文打了分。

derivatives.zh: 由 grade 加 -er 构成，义为「评分者；分选机」
由 grade 加 -ing 构成，义为「评级；分级」
up 与 grade 的复合词，义为「升级」

senses.title: A level of quality or rank
senses.definition: a level of quality, size or rank in a scale
senses.definitionCN: 质量、大小或级别序列中的一档
senses.example: The fruit is sold in three grades in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这种水果在市场按三个等级出售。
senses.why: The core image is one step on a ladder of quality, so the plain sense is a rank.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是质量阶梯上的一级，最基本的义项就是等级。

senses.title: A school year
senses.definition: one year in an American school course
senses.definitionCN: 美国学制中的一学年
senses.example: My cousin is in the sixth grade this year.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟今年上六年级。
senses.why: Learning is climbed step by step, so each year becomes one grade.
senses.whyCN: 学习逐级攀登，每一年就是一级。

senses.title: A mark for schoolwork
senses.definition: a mark or score given for a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 给作业或考试打的分数
senses.example: She got the highest grade in the spelling test.
senses.exampleCN: 她在拼写测验中得了最高分。
senses.why: The rank given to the work becomes the number on the paper.
senses.whyCN: 给作业定下的等级变成纸上的分数。

senses.title: To sort or mark by rank
senses.definition: to give a grade to something, or to sort things by quality
senses.definitionCN: 给某物定级，或按质量分类
senses.example: The teacher graded every essay before the holiday.

senses.title: A slope of a road
senses.definition: the degree of slope of a road or railway
senses.definitionCN: 道路或铁路的倾斜程度
senses.example: The truck slowed on the steep grade of the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在山路陡坡上放慢了速度。
senses.why: A ladder can lean: the steps become a slope measured in degrees.

intro.en: Grade comes from the Latin word for a step, and gradus is its twin.
intro.cn: grade 来自拉丁语「台阶」一词，gradus 是它的孪生形式。

items.en: Latin gradus meant a step, and gradi meant to walk in steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为台阶，gradi 意为迈步。

items.en: Medieval Latin gradus named ranks and degrees in learning and the church.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 gradus 指学界与教会的品级。

items.en: French grade carried the step-and-rank sense into Romance speech.
items.cn: 法语 grade 把台阶与等级义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed grade for ranks and degrees of quality.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 grade，指级别与质量度。

items.en: Modern English added the school year, the mark, the slope and the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了年级、分数、坡度与动词用法。

note.en: The words below resemble grade in sound or share the step-and-rank field.
note.cn: 以下词与 grade 音近，或同属台阶与等级义场。

entries.definition: One who grades, or a grading machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评分者；分选机」，由 grade 直接派生。

entries.definition: To push someone into action; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驱使」，读音与 grade 接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Elegance or divine kindness; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优雅；恩典」，与 grade 仅差一个字母，词源不同。
名词，义为「级别；地位」，对应等级义。

entries.definition: A score given for school work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分数」，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: One movement on a stair or in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「台阶；步骤」，与 grade 的「台阶」本义相近。

normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Latin gradus means a step, also kept in gradual and gradually.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为台阶，gradual 一词仍保留它。

normal.en: Upgrade means to move up one grade or level.
normal.cn: upgrade 指升一级。

normal.en: American schools count years as grades one to twelve.
normal.cn: 美国学校用 grade 计年级，从一到十二。

normal.en: Graded milk carries an official quality rank.
normal.cn: graded milk 带有官方等级标记。

normal.en: A road grade is measured as a slope percentage.
normal.cn: 道路 grade 以坡度百分比衡量。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where each rung holds one quality level.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每级横档代表一个质量等级。

abstract.en: See a red pen writing numbers beside each essay.
abstract.cn: 想象红笔在每篇作文旁写下分数。

abstract.en: Think of a truck crawling up a steep mountain slope.
abstract.cn: 想象卡车缓缓爬上陡峭的山坡。

examples.en: The teacher graded every essay before the holiday.
examples.cn: 老师在假期前给每篇作文打了分。

examples.en: My cousin is in the sixth grade this year.
examples.cn: 我表弟今年上六年级。

examples.en: The truck slowed on the steep grade of the mountain road.
examples.cn: 卡车在山路陡坡上放慢了速度。

root: grade 源自拉丁语 gradus（台阶）、gradi（迈步），经法语进入英语；同根词有 gradual、gradually、upgrade、degrade。

sensesIntro.en: Grade climbs from a quality step to school years, marks, the sorting action and slopes.
sensesIntro.cn: grade 从质量台阶爬升到年级、分数、评定动作与坡度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one step on a ladder of quality
core.cn: 核心意象：质量阶梯上的一级

intro.cn: grade 是拉丁词根的基础词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradus is the direct ancestor, so the Latin step-family is grade's own family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 是直接祖先，台阶词族就是 grade 本族。

definition_zh: 栅栏；篱笆；围栏；击剑运动；把……围起来；闪烁其词
definition_en: a structure made of posts and boards or wire that divides or surrounds an area, the sport of sword fighting, or to surround an area with such a structure
core_image: 一根根木桩连成线，把院子里的世界和外面的世界隔开
scene: 新搬来的邻居正沿着院界把木桩一根根打进土里。 They will fence the yard to keep the dog inside.
sceneCN: 这里 fence 是动词，指「用栅栏把院子围起来」，对应第 4 个义项；句意为他们要给院子装栅栏，把狗关在院内。

pos.zh: 栅栏；篱笆；围栏；击剑运动
用栅栏围起；击剑；回避正面回答

derivatives.zh: 栅栏材料；击剑运动（fence 加 -ing，指围栏材料或剑术运动）
击剑运动员（fence 加施动者后缀 -er）
防御；保卫（与 fence 同源，拉丁语系内表「隔开、挡开」）

senses.title: A barrier around or between areas
senses.definition: a structure of posts, boards or wire that encloses or divides land
senses.definitionCN: 由木桩、木板或铁丝构成，用于围住或分隔土地的结构
senses.example: The horse jumped over the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 马跳过了栅栏。
senses.why: The word means the line itself first: posts joined into a boundary you can see.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指那条线本身：木桩连成看得见的边界。

senses.title: The sport of sword fighting
senses.definition: a sport in which two people fight with long thin swords
senses.definitionCN: 两名选手用细长剑对抗的运动
senses.example: He took up fencing at school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校开始练击剑。
senses.why: Sword fighting grew out of defending a line, so the barrier word named the sport.
senses.whyCN: 剑术源于守住一条线，于是围栏词命名了这项运动。

senses.title: To avoid giving a direct answer
senses.definition: to answer questions in a clever but unclear way
senses.definitionCN: 用巧妙但含糊的方式回答问题
senses.example: The minister fenced when asked about taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 被问到税收时，部长闪烁其词。
senses.why: A fencer parries every blow, so the verb describes dodging every question.
senses.whyCN: 击剑手挡开每一次攻击，动词因此形容躲开每一个问题。

senses.title: To surround an area with a fence
senses.definition: to put a fence around a garden or field
senses.definitionCN: 在花园或田地四周装上栅栏
senses.example: They fenced the yard to keep the dog inside.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给院子装上栅栏，把狗关在里面。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action: putting the line into place.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动作：把那条边界线装到位。

senses.title: To separate off a piece of land
senses.definition: to divide land with a fence, often into a separate part
senses.definitionCN: 用栅栏把土地隔成单独的部分
senses.example: Part of the field was fenced off for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 田地的一部分被隔开进行修缮。
senses.why: A barrier does not only enclose; it also cuts one space away from another.
senses.whyCN: 栅栏不只围住，也把一处空间从另一处切分出来。

intro.en: Fence is a shortened form of defence: the same idea of shielding a line was cut down to name the barrier, then the swordplay behind it.
intro.cn: fence 是 defence 的缩略：同属「挡开、护住一条线」的概念被截短用来命名栅栏，随后又指栅栏后的剑术。

items.en: Latin defendere meant 'to ward off, guard', built from fens, the stem of fendere 'to strike'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 defendere 意为「挡开、守护」，出自 fendere「击打」的词干 fens。

items.en: Old French defence carried the idea of guarding and shielding into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 defence 把守护与遮挡的观念带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English shortened defence to fense, written fence, for a protective barrier.
items.cn: 中古英语把 defence 缩略为 fense，写作 fence，指防护性屏障。

items.en: The barrier sense spread to farms and gardens, and the verb fence meant to enclose.
items.cn: 现代英语里屏障义扩展到农田与花园，动词 fence 表示围起。

items.en: Sword practice and clever parrying gave the sport, the athlete and the evasive answer senses.
items.cn: 剑术练习与巧妙的挡避派生出运动、运动员与回避作答诸义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fence spelling or the fend root; near-meaning words cover barriers and evasion.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fence 拼写或 fend 词根；近义组覆盖屏障与回避两个义场。

entries.definition: the act of protecting; fence is its shortened form
entries.definitionCN: 防御；fence 即其缩略形

entries.definition: a crime or hurt feeling; close in shape but about attacking, not barriers
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪或冒犯；形近而义指冒犯，与屏障无关

entries.definition: a guard against scratches; keeps the fend idea
entries.definitionCN: 防擦护板；保留 fend 的「挡开」义

entries.definition: a row of bushes used as a boundary
entries.definitionCN: 作边界的灌木树篱
分隔空间的实体墙

entries.definitionCN: 回避；躲闪不作正面回答

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the defence root and the classic phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 defence 词根与经典短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fence is defence with the de- sliced off: a fence defends your line.
normal.cn: fence 是 defence 砍掉 de-：栅栏守住你的边界。

normal.en: sit on the fence is the picture of a person sitting on a wall between two sides.
normal.cn: sit on the fence 画面是一个人坐在两侧之间的墙上骑墙观望。

normal.en: fencing is the sport, fencer is the athlete, fence is the sword move.
normal.cn: fencing 是运动，fencer 是运动员，fence 是剑上动作。

normal.en: fence off means to cut a piece of land away with a barrier.
normal.cn: fence off 表示用栅栏把一块地隔出来。

normal.en: to fence in a question is to parry it like a sword blow.
normal.cn: 在问题上 fence in，就像用剑挡开劈来的一击。

abstract.en: A fence is an opinion you can see: it says here, not there.
abstract.cn: 栅栏是一条看得见的立场：宣告这里，而非那里。

abstract.en: Fencing words, like fencing swords, keep the fight going without landing anywhere.
abstract.cn: 闪避的言辞如同击剑的剑，打来打去却从不落在实处。

abstract.en: Every boundary is both a shield and a statement.
abstract.cn: 每一条边界既是盾牌，也是宣告。

examples.en: The sheep escaped through a hole in the fence.
examples.cn: 羊从栅栏的破洞里跑出去了。

examples.en: She fenced off the vegetable patch to protect it from rabbits.
examples.cn: 她用栅栏把菜圃隔开，防止兔子进来。

examples.en: Reporters pressed him for answers, but he kept fencing.
examples.cn: 记者们追问答案，他却一直闪避。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奋死」—— 守卫边界奋死不让 → fence 栅栏；捍卫

sensesIntro.en: From the barrier itself to the sword sport, evasive answers, and the acts of enclosing and dividing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屏障本身到击剑运动、闪避作答，以及围起与隔开两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: posts joined into a visible line that separates inside from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桩连成一条可见的线，隔开内与外。

branches.en: THE SPORT: swordplay born of defence.
THE PARRY: dodging questions like blows.
branches.cn: 挡避：像挡剑一样躲开问题。

branches.en: THE ACT: putting a fence in place.
THE CUT: dividing land into parts.

intro.en: The fence family hangs on the fend root, where defence, offence and their verbs meet.
intro.cn: fence 词族挂在 fend 词根上，defence、offence 及其动词在此交汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin fendere 'to strike' gives the stems; defendere adds the prefix de- 'away'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fendere「击打」提供词干；defendere 加上前缀 de-「离开」。

items.meaning: to strike against; to hurt feelings
items.exampleCN: 他的玩笑冒犯了许多人。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被击打的；fence 的词干来源

definition_zh: 生长；长大；种植；变得；逐渐变成
definition_en: to develop and become larger or taller; to plant and care for something so it develops; to gradually become
core_image: 一粒种子从土里探出头，慢慢拔高，最后长成大树
scene: 奶奶在院子里埋下桃核，每天浇水，看着小苗一点点升高。 The little tree will grow quickly if you water it every day.
sceneCN: 这里 grow 是「生长、长高」（第 1 个义项：生物自然变大）；句意是每天浇水小树就会长得很快。

derivatives.zh: 由 grow 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「生长；增长」
由 grow 加 -er 构成，义为「种植者；栽培者」

senses.title: To develop in size naturally
senses.definition: to get bigger or taller as part of natural development
senses.definitionCN: 作为自然发育过程而变大变高
senses.example: Children grow fast in their first years.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在最初几年长得很快。
senses.why: The picture is a seed pushing upward, so the first sense is simply natural increase.
senses.whyCN: 画面是种子向上顶出土壤，第一个义项就是最直观的自然增大。

senses.title: To plant and raise crops
senses.definition: to put plants in soil and help them develop
senses.definitionCN: 把植物种进土里并帮它发育
senses.example: Farmers here grow vegetables all year round.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民全年种植蔬菜。
senses.why: If you help a plant grow, we say you grow it; the helper borrows the plant's verb.
senses.whyCN: 帮植物长大就说「种植」，帮助者借用了植物的动词。

senses.title: To become gradually
senses.definition: to slowly change into a state or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地进入某种状态或情绪
senses.example: The room grew quiet as the film began.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开场时房间渐渐安静下来。
senses.why: Getting taller happens slowly, so the same slow slide describes changes of feeling or state.
senses.whyCN: 长高是缓慢的过程，这种缓慢的变化同样可以描述状态或情绪的改变。

senses.title: To increase in amount
senses.definition: to become larger in number, amount, or strength
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、规模或力量上变大
senses.example: The city has grown quickly in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间这座城市扩张得很快。
senses.why: Anything that swells like a plant is described with the same upward image.
senses.whyCN: 任何像植物一样膨胀壮大的事物，都借用同一幅向上的画面。

senses.title: To let hair or nails lengthen
senses.definition: to stop cutting so that hair or nails become longer
senses.definitionCN: 停止修剪使头发或指甲变长
senses.example: He is growing a beard for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他冬天打算留胡子。
senses.why: Hair grows by itself; letting it happen makes you the owner of the process.
senses.whyCN: 头发会自己长，任其生长就让养发者成了这一过程的主导者。

intro.en: Grow is a pure Germanic word with a very old farming root.
intro.cn: grow 是纯粹的日耳曼语词，词根古老，与农耕生活相关。

items.en: Old Norse groja meant to green or sprout, related to the green of new plants.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 groja 意为发绿、发芽，与嫩苗的绿色相关。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic root gro- connects growing things with green color.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根 gro- 把「生长之物」与「绿色」联系在一起。

items.en: Old English growan meant to grow, increase, or develop, already used for people, plants, and numbers.
items.cn: 古英语 growan 意为生长、增长、发育，已可用于人、植物和数量。

items.en: Middle English kept the word and added the farming sense of growing crops.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用该词，并增加了种植庄稼的农事义。

items.en: Modern English completed the picture with the linking-verb sense of gradually becoming.
items.cn: 现代英语补全画面，增加了「渐渐变得」的系动词用法。

note.en: Words shaped like grow or close to it in meaning.
note.cn: 与 grow 词形相近或词义相关的词。

entries.definition: the past participle of grow, meaning fully developed
entries.definitionCN: grow 的过去分词，义为「成熟的；长大的」

entries.definition: to grow or change into a bigger or better form
entries.definitionCN: 发展；发育，强调过程变化

entries.definition: to begin to grow, as a bud or shoot
entries.definitionCN: 发芽；抽枝，强调生长的开始

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks for grow.
normalIntro.cn: 五条 grow 的记忆钩子。

normal.en: grew and grown are the two irregular past forms
normal.cn: grew 和 grown 是两个不规则过去形式，一起背。

normal.en: grow up means becoming an adult, grow old means aging
normal.cn: grow up 长大成人，grow old 变老，两句对照记忆。

normal.en: grow and green share the old root of living plants
normal.cn: grow 与 green 同源于有生命植物的老词根。

normal.en: farmers grow crops, gardeners grow flowers
normal.cn: 农民种庄稼、园丁种花，用场景固定动词义。

normal.en: grow tired, grow quiet, grow dark all mean gradually become
normal.cn: grow tired / quiet / dark 都是「渐渐变得」。

abstract.en: a sprout pushing out of dark soil
abstract.cn: 嫩芽顶破黑土，向上生长的画面。

abstract.en: a ruler line climbing year by year
abstract.cn: 身高尺上的刻度逐年上移。

abstract.en: a shadow lengthening as evening comes
abstract.cn: 傍晚影子慢慢拉长，事物渐渐变化。

examples.en: Tomatoes grow best in warm sunny places.
examples.cn: 西红柿在温暖向阳的地方长得最好。

examples.en: She grew more confident after the speech.
examples.cn: 演讲之后她变得更有自信了。

examples.en: My little brother has grown out of his shoes.
examples.cn: 我弟弟长得已经穿不下原来那双鞋了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「割肉」——庄稼割了一茬又长一茬，grow（生长）就是不停往上蹿。

root: 来自古英语 growan，可追溯至原始日耳曼语词根 gro-（生长、变绿），与古诺斯语 groja 同源；核心画面是植物由绿芽开始向上生长。

sensesIntro.en: From natural increase the word extends to farming, gradual change, numeric growth, and even hair.

core.cn: 核心意象：种子向上顶出土壤

intro.cn: grow 本身无前后缀，这一栏展示由它衍生构词的常用部件。

latinIntro.en: Latin-based endings that attach to English verbs like grow.
latinIntro.cn: 可附着于 grow 这类英语动词的拉丁语系词尾。

definition_en: at, to, or from a great distance, or to a great degree
core_image: 地平线上一个越来越小的背影，脚下的路一直铺到眼睛看不清的地方
scene: 站台上望着远去的列车，同学挥手直到看不见为止。 The train rolled away and grew small, going far down the line.
sceneCN: 这里指「远」，对应第 1 个义项：距离遥远；句意为列车沿铁轨驶向远方。画面要点：站台、挥动的手、缩小的列车。

pos.zh: 远的；遥远的；久远的；远端的

derivatives.zh: 更远的（far 的比较级，多指实际距离）
进一步的（比较级，多指程度，也可作动词）
遥远的；恍惚的（复合形容词）
影响深远的（复合形容词）
遥远的（复合形容词）

senses.title: At or to a great distance
senses.definition: at, to, or from a great distance
senses.definitionCN: 在很远的地方，或达到很远的距离
senses.example: The station is not far from here.
senses.exampleCN: 车站离这儿不远。
senses.why: Distance is the root meaning; everything else measures along it.
senses.whyCN: 距离是词根义；其余义项都沿它度量。

senses.title: Much or to a great extent
senses.definition: very much, or to a great degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 非常，或达到很大程度
senses.example: The result is far better than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 结果比预期好得多。
senses.why: Long distance becomes long degree: far maps space onto amount.
senses.whyCN: 长距离变成长程度：far 把空间映射到数量。

senses.title: Distant in time or remote in relation
senses.definition: remote in time, or distant in similarity or connection
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上久远，或在相似与联系上疏远
senses.example: The far past is hard to imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 遥远的过去难以想象。
senses.why: Space stretches into time and into how closely things are tied.
senses.whyCN: 空间延伸为时间，也延伸为事物联系的紧密程度。

senses.title: The far side or end
senses.definition: more distant of two, as in the far side or far end
senses.definitionCN: 两者中较远的，如 far side、far end
senses.example: He sat at the far end of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐在桌子远端。
senses.why: Among two distances, far picks the longer one.
senses.whyCN: 在两个距离之间，far 挑出更长的那个。

intro.en: Far is a native English adverb and adjective, straight from Old English feorr, with Germanic cousins everywhere.
intro.cn: far 是英语本族的副词兼形容词，直接出自古英语 feorr，在日耳曼诸语中亲戚遍地。

items.en: The reconstructed root ferhaz meant far, distant; the same root gives German fern.
items.cn: 重构词根 ferhaz 意为远的；德语 fern 同根。

items.en: Old English feorr served as both adjective and adverb: a feorr land, to travel feorr.
items.cn: 古英语 feorr 兼作形容词与副词：远方的土地、远行。

items.en: Middle English far and ferre kept both uses; comparatives ferther, farther grew from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 far、ferre 保留两种用法，并长出 farther、further。

items.en: Early Modern English fixed far as the positive of farther and further.
items.cn: 早期现代英语把 far 定为 farther、further 的原级。

items.en: Modern English spread far into phrases: far away, so far, far from it.
items.cn: 现代英语让 far 走进无数短语：far away、so far、far from it。

note.en: Look-alikes share the single syllable; near-meaning words name distances and degrees of remoteness.
note.cn: 形近组共享单音节外形；近义组命名距离与疏远的程度。

entries.definitionCN: 介词；拼写相近，读音不同
旅费；元音与 far 不同
毛皮；拼写相近但无关

entries.definition: far away in space or time
entries.definitionCN: 遥远的；更书面
偏远的；强调隔绝
遥远地；微弱地

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the shortest distance word.
normalIntro.cn: 最短的「距离」词，五个抓手。

normal.en: far has two comparatives: farther for distance, further for degree.
normal.cn: far 有两个比较级：farther 指距离，further 指程度。

normal.en: so far means up to now: the best results so far.
normal.cn: so far 意为「到目前为止」。

normal.en: by far picks the clear winner: the best by far.
normal.cn: by far 表示「远远地」：遥遥领先。

normal.en: far from it means the opposite is true.
normal.cn: far from it 表示「恰恰相反」。

normal.en: German fern is a cousin of far.
normal.cn: 德语 fern 与 far 同源。

abstract.en: Distance is the mind's ruler; far is where the ruler runs out.
abstract.cn: 距离是心里的尺子；far 是尺子刻度穷尽之处。

abstract.en: Some goals are far, not in kilometers but in years.
abstract.cn: 有些目标之远，不在公里，而在年月。

abstract.en: The far past is a country with no roads left.
abstract.cn: 遥远的过去是一个没有路可通的国度。

examples.en: The hospital is far from the village.
examples.cn: 医院离村子很远。

examples.en: This is by far the best answer.
examples.cn: 这显然是最好的答案。

examples.en: The plan is far from perfect.
examples.cn: 这个计划远非完美。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法」——法官传唤远方证人，来回路途法（far）定很远。

root: 古英语 feorr（远），出自原始日耳曼语 ferhaz，与德语 fern 同族。本族词，兼作形容词与副词；比较级 farther/further、最高级 farthest/furthest。词义由空间距离延伸到程度、时间与关系。

sensesIntro.en: From spatial distance outward to degree, time, relation, and the far end of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从空间距离扩展到程度、时间、关系与事物的远端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that keeps going after your eyes give up.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛看不清之后仍在延伸的路。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE: the root spatial sense.
THE DEGREE: much, as measured on the distance ruler.
branches.cn: 程度：用距离尺子度量的「多」。

branches.en: THE REMOTE: distant times and loose ties.
branches.cn: 疏远：久远的时间与松散的联系。

branches.en: THE FAR END: the more distant of two.
THE RULER: one scale for both space and amount.
branches.cn: 尺子：空间与数量共用同一刻度。

intro.en: Far is a bare Germanic root; its family grows through comparatives and compounds.
intro.cn: far 是裸的日耳曼词根；词族靠比较级与复合词生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no member of this Germanic family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个日耳曼词族中没有成员。

items.meaning: to a greater degree or distance

definition_zh: 每件事；一切；所有事物；最重要的事
definition_en: all things; every single thing
core_image: 一张写满的清单：每一行都打了勾
scene: 露营前一晚，妈妈把装备一件件摆上桌。 We packed everything we needed for the camping trip.
sceneCN: 这里 everything 是「一切」（第 1 个义项：所有事物）；句意是我们打包了露营所需的一切。

derivatives.zh: 同族代词，指人，义为「每个人」
同族副词，指地点，义为「到处」
基础词，义为「事物；东西」

senses.title: All things
senses.definition: every single thing in a group or situation, followed by a singular verb
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或情境中的每一件事，后接单数动词
senses.example: Everything in the room was covered with dust.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的每样东西都蒙着灰。
senses.why: The word walks a full checklist, then seals it into one single bundle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词走完整张清单，再把它们封成一束。

senses.title: The most important thing
senses.definition: the thing that matters most, often in mean everything to someone
senses.definitionCN: 最重要的事，常见于 mean everything to someone
senses.example: Her little brother means everything to her.
senses.exampleCN: 弟弟对她来说就是一切。
senses.why: When one item outweighs the whole list, everything shrinks to that single treasure.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事重过整张清单，everything 便缩为那唯一的珍宝。

intro.en: Everything joins every with the Old English word thing, which once meant an assembly and then any matter discussed there.
intro.cn: everything 由 every 与古英语 thing 结合，thing 原指集会，后指会上讨论的任何事务。

items.en: Old English thing meant a meeting or assembly, where matters were settled.
items.cn: 古英语 thing 指集会，人们在会上处理事务。

items.en: The word then narrowed to any matter or object discussed or dealt with.
items.cn: 词义随后收窄为任何被讨论、处理的事物。

items.en: Middle English thing was ready to compound, and every supplied the total sweep.
items.cn: 中古英语 thing 可参与复合，every 提供全覆盖的扫掠。

items.en: Everything appeared as a pronoun beside everyone and everybody.
items.cn: everything 作为代词与 everyone、everybody 并列出现。

items.en: The emotional use, meaning everything to someone, grew in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「对某人意义重于一切」的情感用法在口语中生长。

note.en: The first group collects the every-compound family; the second collects near meanings about totality.
note.cn: 第一组收集 every 复合词族；第二组收集与「全部」相关的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 每个人。指人不指物。

entries.definition: any thing at all, used in questions and negatives
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物。用于疑问句与否定句。

entries.definition: no thing at all; the direct opposite
entries.definitionCN: 什么都没有。直接反义词。

entries.definition: the whole amount, works for people and things
entries.definitionCN: 全部。可用于人与物，接复数动词。
全部（口语）。英式口语表达。
所有提到的那些。指代前文内容。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks built from the thing root and packing scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于 thing 词根与打包场景的具体联想。

normal.en: Every plus thing builds the word, counting each single item.
normal.cn: everything＝every＋thing，每一件「thing」都算。

normal.en: Thing once meant an assembly matter, so it covers things and events.
normal.cn: thing 古义是集会上议的事，所以指物也指事。

normal.en: Everything is ready is the calmest line before a trip.
normal.cn: Everything is ready 出发前最安心的一句话。

normal.en: Compare everything, anything and nothing as a triangle.
normal.cn: 对比三角：everything、anything、nothing 一正一疑一反。

normal.en: The sound hints at gathering every star on a list, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「爱夫瑞星」——把每颗星都收进清单，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture a packed suitcase with every item ticked off.
abstract.cn: 画面：行李箱装满，清单上每项都打勾。

abstract.en: Sweep the desk clean into one neat drawer.
abstract.cn: 动作：把桌面一扫收进一个整齐抽屉。

abstract.en: Feel a warm weight, like carrying the whole of home.
abstract.cn: 感觉：怀抱如家一般全部的温暖重量。

examples.en: Everything on the menu looks delicious.
examples.cn: 菜单上的每样东西看起来都很好吃。

examples.en: Don't worry; everything will be fine.
examples.cn: 别担心，一切都会好起来的。

examples.en: Our dog means everything to our family.
examples.cn: 我们的狗对全家来说就是一切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱夫瑞星」——把每颗星都收进清单，谐音帮助拼读，不是词源。

root: everything 由 every 加 thing 构成；thing 源自古英语，原指集会，后指事务与物件。本词与 everyone、everywhere 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Everything seals all things into one bundle, and can even shrink to the single thing that matters most.
sensesIntro.cn: everything 先把万物封作一束，也能缩为最重要的一件事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full checklist with every line ticked.
core.cn: 核心意象：每一行都打勾的完整清单。

branches.cn: 房间里的每样东西都蒙着灰。

intro.en: Everything compounds every with thing; its siblings point to people and places.
intro.cn: everything 由 every 复合 thing；同辈词分别指向人与地点。

latinIntro.cn: 本词与拉丁词根无关，词族属于日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词列表为空。

items.meaning: an object or matter, once an assembly
items.example: Old English thing meant a meeting.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 thing 指集会。

items.example: Everyone and everything mirror each other.
items.exampleCN: everyone 与 everything 相互对应。

items.example: There is something in my shoe.
Pack the tent first, then everything else.
items.exampleCN: 先装帐篷，再装其他一切。

items.example: What is that thing on the table?

definition_zh: 死；死亡；终结；消亡
definition_en: the end of the life of a person or living thing
core_image: 生命之灯缓缓熄灭的那一刻
scene: 科学课上我们观察了一颗种子如何结束休眠。 The death of the old tree left a sunny space for young plants.
sceneCN: 这里 death 是「消亡」（第 2 个义项：事物的终结）；句意是老树的枯亡给幼苗留出了阳光。

collocations.phrase: the death of an old custom

derivatives.zh: death 的同族动词，义为「死」
由 die 词族派生的形容词，义为「死的」
由 dead 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「致命的」
die 的现在分词形式，义为「垂死的」

senses.title: The end of life
senses.definition: the moment or state when a person or animal stops living
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物停止生命的时刻或状态
senses.example: The death of the class hamster made everyone sad.
senses.exampleCN: 仓鼠的死让全班同学都很难过。
senses.why: Life is a flame; when the flame goes out, the ending needs a word of its own.
senses.whyCN: 生命像一盏灯，灯火熄灭的时刻需要一个专属的名字，于是有了 death 这个词。

senses.title: The end or ruin of something
senses.definition: the end of an activity, idea or custom
senses.definitionCN: 某种活动、观念或习俗的结束
senses.example: The death of that old tradition took many years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个旧传统的消亡花了许多年。
senses.why: When a thing stops forever, we speak of it like a life ending.
senses.whyCN: 一件事彻底停止时，我们像谈论生命结束一样谈论它，死亡义便借给了终结。

senses.title: Great degree, in phrases
senses.definition: used in phrases to show the strongest degree
senses.definitionCN: 在短语中表示最高程度
senses.example: The funny film made us laugh to death.
senses.exampleCN: 那部搞笑电影让我们笑死了。
senses.why: A feeling so strong it fills the whole body borrows the image of a total ending.
senses.whyCN: 强烈到极致的感觉借用了「彻底终结」的画面，仿佛情绪满到把人整个填满。

intro.en: Death grew from an old Germanic word for dying.
intro.cn: death 由一个表示「死去」的古老日耳曼词生长而来。

items.en: The word death meant dying or the end of life.
items.cn: 古英语 death 意为死去或生命的终结。

items.en: It shares a root with words for dying across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 它与日耳曼语族中各语言表示「死」的词共享词根。

items.en: The spelling became deth and then death in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 十三世纪拼写从 deth 变为 death。

items.en: Writers used it not only for people but for the end of kingdoms and customs.
items.cn: 作家不仅用它指人的死亡，也指王国与习俗的终结。

items.en: Fixed phrases like laugh to death and death rate keep it busy today.
items.cn: 现代英语中 laugh to death、death rate 等固定短语仍在频繁使用。

note.en: These words stand around death, from its verb to its near neighbours.
note.cn: 这些词围绕 death，从它的同族动词到近邻概念。

死的
致命的

normalIntro.en: Use the flame image and the die family to remember death.
normalIntro.cn: 用「灯灭」的画面和 die 词族记住 death。

normal.en: die is the verb, death is the noun.
normal.cn: die 是动词，death 是名词。

normal.en: dead is the adjective: the tree is dead.
normal.cn: 形容词是 dead：the tree is dead（树死了）。

normal.en: deadly means able to kill.
normal.cn: deadly 表示能致命的。

normal.en: th at the end: death, teeth, breath.
normal.cn: 词尾是 th：death、teeth、breath。

normal.en: laugh to death is a friendly exaggeration.
normal.cn: laugh to death 是友好的夸张说法。

abstract.en: See a candle's flame shrink to one point and go dark.
abstract.cn: 想象烛火缩成一点然后暗下去。

abstract.en: Hear the long h at the end of death, like a soft breath.
abstract.cn: 听 death 结尾长长的 h，像一声轻轻的呼气。

abstract.en: Feel how a custom fades slowly, like a light going out.
abstract.cn: 体会习俗慢慢淡去的感觉，如同灯一点点熄灭。

examples.en: The death of the goldfish taught us to say goodbye.
examples.cn: 金鱼的死教会了我们如何道别。

examples.en: The old bridge's death came when the river changed course.
examples.cn: 河流改道后，那座老桥的使命终结了。

examples.en: My grandpa's stories nearly made us laugh to death.
examples.cn: 爷爷的故事差点把我们笑死。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得死」——灯灭人走，「得死」谐音提醒这是「死亡」

root: 来自古英语 death，与动词 die 同属日耳曼语族的死词族；名词由古英语词根 dēa-（死去）加 -th（名词后缀）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Death names life's ending, then lends that ending to customs and strong feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: death 先指生命的终结，再把这个终结借给习俗的消亡和极致的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a life flame going out
core.cn: 核心意象：生命之火熄灭

branches.en: A feeling pushed to the top

branches.cn: 所有终结共享那份寂静
强烈的表达借用彻底的终结

intro.en: Death is built with an old noun ending on a dying root.
intro.cn: death 由表示「死」的词根加古老的名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Death is Germanic, so it has no Latin relatives here.
latinIntro.cn: death 属日耳曼语源，这里没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 摇动；动摇；发抖；握手；奶昔
definition_en: to move quickly from side to side, to make someone uncertain, to tremble, to hold hands in greeting, or a thick milk drink
core_image: 瓶子在手中上下晃动，里面的液体撞出细响
scene: 她打开瓶子前摇了摇。 She shook the bottle before opening it.
sceneCN: 这里 shake 是「摇动」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她打开瓶子前摇了摇。

derivatives.zh: 摇晃的；不牢靠的
摇酒器
震惊的
摇动；颤抖

senses.title: To move quickly
senses.definition: to move something quickly up and down or side to side
senses.definitionCN: 使某物快速上下或左右移动
senses.example: She shook the bottle before opening it.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开瓶子前摇了摇。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To weaken confidence
senses.definition: to make someone feel uncertain or upset
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到不确定或不安
senses.example: The news shook her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。
senses.why: A shock can shake the mind.
senses.whyCN: 冲击能摇动内心。

senses.title: To tremble
senses.definition: to tremble with cold, fear, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或情绪而颤抖
senses.example: He shook with cold.
senses.exampleCN: 他冷得发抖。
senses.why: The body shakes when it loses steadiness.
senses.whyCN: 身体失去稳定时就会发抖。

senses.title: To greet with hands
senses.definition: to hold and move someone's hand as a greeting
senses.definitionCN: 以握住并摇动对方的手来表示问候
senses.example: They shook hands at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口握了手。
senses.why: The gesture moves the joined hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个手势让相握的手摇动。

senses.title: Milk drink
senses.definition: a thick drink of milk and ice cream
senses.definitionCN: 由牛奶和冰淇淋摇匀的浓稠饮料
senses.example: He ordered a chocolate shake.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯巧克力奶昔。
senses.why: The drink is shaken before serving.
senses.whyCN: 这种饮料在供应前要摇匀。

intro.en: Shake comes from Old English sceacan, to move with a quick back-and-forth motion.
intro.cn: shake 源自古英语 sceacan，意为快速来回移动。

items.en: Skakan meant to shake.

items.en: Sceacan meant to move quickly.
items.cn: sceacan 意为快速移动。

items.en: Shake kept the same motion.
items.cn: shake 保留了同样的动作。

items.en: Shake named a greeting with hands.
items.cn: shake 指握手的问候。

items.en: Shake named a thick milk drink.
items.cn: shake 指浓稠的奶制饮料。

note.en: Shake is compared with similar-looking words and with words for trembling and moving.
note.cn: 把 shake 与形近词以及表示颤抖和移动的词作比较。

entries.definitionCN: 阴凉处
形状
分享
颤抖

entries.definition: to move rapidly back and forth
entries.definitionCN: 振动
搅动

normalIntro.en: Shake moves from the bottle to the voice, the body, the hand, and the glass.
normalIntro.cn: shake 从瓶子一路摇到声音、身体、手和杯子。

normal.en: Shake the juice before drinking.
normal.cn: 喝果汁前先摇一摇。

normal.en: The bad news shook the whole team.
normal.cn: 坏消息震动了整个团队。

normal.en: She was shaking with fear.
normal.cn: 她吓得发抖。

normal.en: They shook hands and smiled.
normal.cn: 他们握手微笑。

normal.en: He drank a strawberry shake.
normal.cn: 他喝了一杯草莓奶昔。

abstract.en: To shake is to interrupt steadiness for a moment.
abstract.cn: 摇动，就是短暂地打断稳定。

abstract.en: A handshake can carry more truth than a speech.
abstract.cn: 一次握手，可能比一段话更真实。

abstract.en: What shakes us also shows what holds us.
abstract.cn: 摇动我们的东西，也显出我们被什么托住。

examples.en: She shook the bottle before opening it.
examples.cn: 她打开瓶子前摇了摇。

examples.en: The news shook her confidence.
examples.cn: 这个消息动摇了她的信心。

examples.en: They shook hands at the door.
examples.cn: 他们在门口握了手。

dict_mnemonic.text: shake 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），核心义「来回快速移动」，引申出动摇、发抖与握手。

root: 源自古英语 sceacan（摇动），与德语 schütteln 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shake means to move quickly, to weaken confidence, to tremble, to greet with hands, or a milk drink.
sensesIntro.cn: shake 意为摇动、动摇、发抖、握手或奶昔。

core.en: A quick back-and-forth movement.
core.cn: 快速的来回移动。

branches.en: A body that cannot stay still.

intro.en: Shake is a strong native verb with irregular past forms.
intro.cn: shake 是日耳曼语本族强变化动词，过去式不规则。

latinIntro.en: Shake has no Latin ancestor; Latin quatere, to shake, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shake 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 quatere（摇动）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He was shaken by the news.
She filled the shaker with ice.

definition_zh: 五十；五十个（人、物）；五十年代；五十岁
definition_en: the number 50, or a group of fifty; also the fifties, the decade of years, or the age of fifty
core_image: 一张五十面额的纸币在指间被数过
scene: 颁奖礼上主持人念出获奖者的执教年限。 The coach has watched fifty seasons of football pass.
sceneCN: 这里 fifty 是数词，指「五十」这一数目，对应第 1 个义项；句意为这位教练已看过五十个赛季的足球。

forms.label: 复数（五十年代；五十多岁）

derivatives.zh: 第五十（fifty 加序数后缀 -eth，指第五十个）
五十年代；五十多岁（fifty 的复数形式，指年份或年龄段）
五十倍的（fifty 加 -fold，指五十倍的程度）

senses.title: The number 50
senses.definition: the number between forty-nine and fifty-one
senses.definitionCN: 四十九与五十一之间的数目
senses.example: The hall seats fifty people.
senses.exampleCN: 礼堂可容纳五十人。
senses.why: Five tens laid end to end make the round half-hundred.
senses.whyCN: 五个十首尾相接，便是圆满的半百。

senses.title: The age of fifty
senses.definition: the age of fifty years
senses.definitionCN: 年届五十的年纪
senses.example: At fifty he finally opened his own shop.
senses.exampleCN: 五十岁时他终于开了自己的店。
senses.why: Numbers mark life's milestones as surely as they count sheep.
senses.whyCN: 数字既能数羊，也能标记人生节点。

senses.title: The decade of the fifties
senses.definition: the years from fifty to fifty-nine in a century
senses.definitionCN: 一个世纪中五十到五十九的十年
senses.example: The band plays hits from the fifties.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演奏五十年代的金曲。
senses.why: Plural years turn a number into an era.
senses.whyCN: 年份的复数形式把数字变成时代。

senses.title: An even split
senses.definition: an equal share, as in fifty-fifty
senses.definitionCN: 相等的份额，如 fifty-fifty
senses.example: Let us split the bill fifty-fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 我们平摊账单吧。
senses.why: Half of a hundred is the picture of perfect fairness.
senses.whyCN: 一百的一半正是绝对公平的画面。

intro.en: Fifty is the Germanic compound five-plus-ten at the tens level: five tens, spoken as one word since Old English.
intro.cn: fifty 是「五加十」在十位层面的日耳曼复合词：五个十，自古英语起读作一词。

items.en: Germanic tens were built by adding a plural ten-suffix to the unit number.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的整十数由基数加复数的「十」后缀构成。

items.en: Old English fiftig meant 'five tens', with stress on the first part.
items.cn: 古英语 fiftig 意为「五个十」，重音在前部。

items.en: Middle English fifty kept the front stress, setting it apart from fifteen.
items.cn: 中古英语 fifty 保留前重音，与 fifteen 区分开来。

items.en: The ordinal fiftieth and the plural fifties completed the family.
items.cn: 现代英语补齐序数 fiftieth 与复数 fifties。

items.en: Fifty-fifty became the everyday idiom of an even split.
items.cn: fifty-fifty 成为日常表达「各半」的习语。

note.en: Look-alikes share the five root or the -ty ending; near-meaning words count the same zone.
note.cn: 形近组共享 five 词根或 -ty 后缀；近义组在同数量区间。

entries.definition: the number 15; stress falls last, unlike fifty
entries.definitionCN: 数字十五；重音在后，与 fifty 不同
第十五位
第五十位

entries.definition: fifty years said as a fraction
entries.definitionCN: 以分数表达的五十年

entries.definition: the fifties as a decade shorthand
entries.definitionCN: 五十年代的缩略说法

entries.definition: at the middle point, like fifty percent
entries.definitionCN: 在中点，如百分之五十

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the tens family and idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自整十词族与习语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fifty = five tens: FIF + TY, stress first.
normal.cn: fifty = 五个十：FIF + TY，重音在前。

normal.en: fifty-fifty is the easiest fairness deal in English.
normal.cn: fifty-fifty 是英语里最简单的公平分法。

normal.en: in his fifties means between fifty and fifty-nine years old.
normal.cn: in his fifties 指五十到五十九岁之间。

normal.en: never write fifty as fivety; the v disappears before t.
normal.cn: 别把 fifty 写成 fivety；t 前 v 消失。

normal.en: a fiftieth birthday party marks fifty full years.
normal.cn: fiftieth 生日派对纪念整整五十岁。

abstract.en: Half a hundred is a doorframe: before it, youth; after it, wisdom.
abstract.cn: 半百是一道门框：门前是青春，门后是智慧。

abstract.en: A fifty-fifty split is the cleanest line fairness can draw.
abstract.cn: 对半分是公平所能画出的最干净的一条线。

abstract.en: Decades are numbers wearing era costumes.
abstract.cn: 年代是穿着时代戏装的数字。

examples.en: More than fifty students signed up for the contest.
examples.cn: 五十多名学生报名参加了比赛。

examples.en: The company celebrated its fiftieth anniversary with a gala.
examples.cn: 公司以庆典庆祝五十周年。

examples.en: The odds are about fifty-fifty for either team.
examples.cn: 两队获胜概率大约各半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「匪付提」—— 五十张钞票匪徒也要分，fifty-fifty 各付一半 → fifty 五十

root: 由古英语 fiftig「五个十」构成，five 加整十后缀 -tig；与 fifteen 的差别在于重音位置与词尾史。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare number to the age, the decade, and the even fifty-fifty split.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的数目到年龄、年代，以及各半的对分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: five tens laid out in a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：五个十排成一行。

branches.en: THE DECADE: the fifties as an era.
branches.cn: 年代：作为时代的五十年代。
里程碑：五十周年的纪念。

intro.en: The -ty family runs from twenty to ninety, all built on unit numbers.
intro.cn: -ty 词族从 twenty 贯穿到 ninety，全部基于基数词。

latinIntro.en: Latin uses quinquaginta for fifty, a different root from the Germanic build.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quinquaginta 表五十，与日耳曼构词不同源。

items.example: The fiftieth customer won a prize.

items.exampleCN: 时尚复兴了五十年代风格。

definition_zh: 美丽地；优美地；出色地
definition_en: in a beautiful way, or very well
core_image: 舞台的灯光落在舞者身上，动作轻而准确
scene: 学校演出时，她在台上跳完一支舞，动作又轻又准。 She danced beautifully at the school show.
sceneCN: 这里 beautifully 是「优美地」（第 1 个义项：以美丽动人的方式）；句意为她在学校演出上跳得很优美。

pos.zh: 副词：美丽地；优美地；出色地

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「美丽的」，beautifully 由它加 -ly 构成
同族名词，义为「美；美人」
同族动词，义为「使变美；美化」

senses.title: In a beautiful way
senses.definition: in a way that is beautiful to see or hear
senses.definitionCN: 以看起来或听起来很美的方式
senses.example: She danced beautifully at the school show.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校演出上跳得很优美。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective beautiful into the manner of an action, so the first sense describes how something is done.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 beautiful 变成动作的方式，所以第一义描述事情做得如何。

senses.title: Very well
senses.definition: in a very skillful or excellent way
senses.definitionCN: 以非常熟练或出色的方式
senses.example: He played the piano beautifully.
senses.exampleCN: 他钢琴弹得很出色。
senses.why: An action done perfectly looks as right as a beautiful object, so the word also praises skill.
senses.whyCN: 做得完美的动作与美的物体一样恰到好处，所以这个词也用来称赞技艺。

intro.en: Beautifully is beautiful plus the old adverb suffix -ly, and its root reaches back to Latin bellus.
intro.cn: beautifully 是 beautiful 加古老的副词后缀 -ly，词根可上溯到拉丁语 bellus。

items.en: Latin bellus meant pretty or fine, probably from a small form of bonus, good.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 意为「漂亮的、美好的」，可能来自 bonus「好」的小称形式。

items.en: The noun for beauty passed through Old French into English as beauty.
items.cn: 表示「美」的名词经古法语以 beauty 进入英语。

items.en: English formed the adjective beautiful by adding -ful to beauty.
items.cn: 英语给 beauty 加上 -ful，构成了形容词 beautiful。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly goes back to Old English -lice, meaning in the manner of.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 可追溯到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」。

items.en: Beautifully is recorded from the later Middle English period; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: beautifully 在中古英语后期已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the beauty family; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of manner and praise.
note.cn: 形近组收 beauty 词族；近义组收其他方式副词与称赞用语。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning very pleasing to see or hear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「美丽的、优美的」，是 beautifully 的基础词。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being beautiful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美」，是这个词族的根名词。
动词，义为「美化、使变美」。

entries.definition: In a dutiful way; it shares the -ful plus -ly ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽职地」，词尾同样是 -ful 加 -ly，但词根不同。

entries.definition: In a good or skillful way; the plain word for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「好、很好地」，是第二个义项最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: With smooth, elegant movement; close to the first sense for bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「优雅地」，形容动作流畅，接近第一义用于身体时的意思。

entries.definition: In a magnificent or excellent way; stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「壮丽地、极好地」，语气更强也更正式。

entries.definition: In a way that has no faults; it stresses accuracy rather than beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完美地」，强调没有差错，而不强调美感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real pieces of the word: beautiful plus -ly, and the family behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实构件：beautiful 加 -ly，以及它背后的词族。

normal.en: Beautiful plus -ly describes the manner, so danced beautifully tells how she danced.
normal.cn: beautiful 加 -ly 描述方式，所以 danced beautifully 说明她跳得怎样。

normal.en: The adverb never compares beauty itself; it only says an action was done in that way.
normal.cn: 这个副词并不比较美本身，只说明动作是以那种方式完成的。

normal.en: Beau-ti-ful-ly has four beats, and the stress stays on the first syllable.
normal.cn: beau-ti-ful-ly 有四个音节，重音仍在第一个音节上。

normal.en: Beautifully made and beautifully written describe the result of careful work.
normal.cn: beautifully made 与 beautifully written 都形容用心做出来的结果。

normal.en: Played beautifully means played very well, which is the second sense.
normal.cn: played beautifully 意为弹得很好，正是第二个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a dancer finishing a turn and holding still: the stillness is as important as the movement.
abstract.cn: 想象舞者转完一圈后定住：那份静止与动作本身同样重要。

abstract.en: An adverb does not change the thing; it changes the way we see the thing being done.
abstract.cn: 副词不改变事物本身，只改变我们看待那件事如何被完成的方式。

abstract.en: The same word praises a dance, a sentence, and a well-made chair, because all three feel finished.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能称赞一支舞、一句话和一把做得很好的椅子，因为三者都显得完整。

examples.en: She danced beautifully at the school show.
examples.cn: 她在学校演出上跳得很优美。

examples.en: He played the piano beautifully.
examples.cn: 他钢琴弹得很出色。

examples.en: The little garden is beautifully simple.
examples.cn: 这个小花园简洁而美。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「标体否离」——标致的身形离不开优美的动作：优美地

root: beautifully 由 beautiful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 来自古英语 -lice「以……方式」。beautiful 由 beauty 加 -ful「充满」构成，beauty 经古法语 beauté 上溯到拉丁语 bellus「漂亮的」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses of beautifully share one manner: doing something in a way that pleases, whether the pleasure is beauty or sheer skill.
sensesIntro.cn: beautifully 的两个义项共用一种「方式」：以令人愉悦的方式完成某事，愉悦可以来自美感，也可以来自纯熟的技艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dancer holds a perfect line under a single light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束灯光下，舞者定出一个完美的线条。

branches.en: THE MANNER: the suffix -ly makes the word describe how an action is done.
branches.cn: 方式线：后缀 -ly 让这个词描述动作是怎样完成的。

branches.en: THE BEAUTY: the action itself is pleasing to watch or hear.
branches.cn: 美感线：动作本身看起来或听起来令人愉悦。

branches.en: THE SKILL: a perfectly done action earns the same word as a beautiful object.
branches.cn: 技艺线：完成得完美的动作，与美的物体得到同一个词。

branches.en: THE CARE: beautifully made things show steady, careful work.
branches.cn: 用心线：做得精美的东西显出稳定而细致的工夫。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the word often appears beside made, written, and played.
branches.cn: 结果线：这个词常与 made、written、played 连用。

intro.en: Beautifully is a transparent formation: a Latin-derived adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: beautifully 是结构透明的构词：拉丁来源的形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin bellus and Late Latin bellitas are recorded and lie behind the beauty family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bellus 与晚期拉丁语 bellitas 均有记录，是 beauty 词族的来源。

items.example: The beauty of the song moved us.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌的美打动了我们。

items.meaning: very pleasing to see or hear
in a beautiful or skillful way

items.exampleCN: 它由 beauty 构成 beautify。
它与 beautifully 构成比较级。

definition_zh: 文本；正文；课文；文字材料；发短信
definition_en: the written words of a book or document as opposed to pictures or notes, or to send someone a written message on a phone
core_image: 一张纸上一行行真正的字：不是边角的批注，而是正文本身
scene: 课堂上老师让大家先看图再看字。 Read the text on page ten before answering the questions.
sceneCN: 这里 text 是「课文；正文」（第 1 个义项：书页上与图片、注释相对的正文文字）；句意：答题前先读第十页的课文。

derivatives.zh: 文本的；正文的（text 加形容词后缀 -ual 构成）
质地；纹理（同出拉丁 texere「编织」，指织出来的手感）
上下文；语境（con- 加 texere 词根，指与正文织在一起的周边文字）
教科书（text 与 book 复合）

senses.title: The main written words
senses.definition: the actual words of a book, article or document, as opposed to pictures, tables or notes
senses.definitionCN: 书、文章或文件的正文文字，与图片、表格或注释相对
senses.example: Look at the picture first, then read the text beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 先看图，再读旁边的正文。
senses.why: The word separates what is woven from what is added: the main cloth of words against the trimmings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「织出来的」与「附加的」分开：正文的字布相对于边角装饰。

senses.title: A written work studied as literature
senses.definition: a written work treated as an object of study, especially in literary or religious criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被当作研究对象的书，尤用于文学或宗教批评
senses.example: Students compare two ancient texts of the same poem.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们比较同一首诗的两个古文本。
senses.why: Once words are fixed in writing, the fixed thing itself can be handled, compared and argued over as a text.
senses.whyCN: 文字一经写定，写定的东西本身就可被当作文本摆弄、比较、争论。

senses.title: A message on a phone
senses.definition: a written message sent by mobile phone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机发送的书面讯息
senses.example: I got a text from her an hour ago.
senses.exampleCN: 一小时前我收到了她的短信。
senses.why: The smallest modern text: written words stripped down to fit a screen and a thumb.
senses.whyCN: 最小的现代「文本」：被屏幕和拇指削到极简的书面语。

senses.title: To send a text message
senses.definition: to send someone a written message using a mobile phone
senses.definitionCN: 用手机给某人发书面讯息
senses.example: Text me when you arrive at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 到车站后给我发短信。
senses.why: The noun moves into verb position the way English loves: the message names the act of sending it.
senses.whyCN: 名词顺势转成动词：讯息之名加给了发送的动作。

senses.title: A passage quoted or used as basis
senses.definition: a short passage from a book, especially one chosen as the subject of a talk or sermon
senses.definitionCN: 书中的短段文字，尤指被选作演讲或布道主题者
senses.example: The priest chose a text from John's gospel for the sermon.
senses.exampleCN: 牧师从约翰福音里选了段经文作讲道底本。
senses.why: A chosen passage stands alone as the base the speaker weaves the talk around.
senses.whyCN: 被选出的段落独立出来，成为讲话者围绕编织的底本。

intro.en: Text is woven: Latin texere meant to weave, and textus was the fabric of a discourse, the thing woven out of words. The weaving image survives in texture and context too.
intro.cn: text 是「织」出来的：拉丁语 texere 意为编织，textus 是话语织成的布料。织的意象同样活在 texture 与 context 里。

items.en: Texere meant to weave, and textus named the woven thing, later the tissue of a written argument.
items.cn: texere 意为编织，textus 指织成之物，后指写成的论证之「织体」。

items.en: The same root gives texture, the feel of weave, and context, the words woven together with a passage.
items.cn: 同一词根给出 texture（织物的手感）与 context（与段落织在一起的前后文字）。

items.en: Old French texte carried the Latin word in the sense of the authoritative wording of scripture.
items.cn: 古法语 texte 承接拉丁词，指圣经经文的权威字句。

items.en: English took text in the 14th century, first for the scriptural passage behind a sermon, then for any body of writing.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪借入 text，先指布道所依的经文段，后泛指一切书面文字。

items.en: Printing, criticism and finally the mobile phone extended the word to any written matter and to texting.
items.cn: 印刷、文学批评，最后是手机，把这个词扩展到一切书面材料与「发短信」。

note.en: The first group collects the weaving family that text belongs to; the second separates text from neighbouring writing words.
note.cn: 第一组收拢 text 所属的「编织」词族；第二组把 text 与相邻的书写类词分开。
